Title: API unit test suite crashes on a clean clone (no .env): service-context.test.ts exits via env.ts process.exit(1)
Environment: E1 local, macOS, Node 26.10, clean `npm ci`, no apps/api/.env
Repro steps:
1. Fresh clone, `npm ci`
2. `npm run build -w @canavo/shared`
3. `npm test` (no apps/api/.env)
Expected: All unit tests pass without secrets or a database — unit tests must be hermetic
Actual: `@canavo/api:test  FAIL src/services/service-context.test.ts — Error: process.exit unexpectedly called with "1" ❯ src/env.ts:43`; 13 tests never ran; turbo exits 1. CI passes only because it injects env vars.
Test ID: existing service-context.test.ts (13 tests) + `env -i … npx vitest run`
Notes: Fix: apps/api/vitest.config.ts supplies test-only dummy env vars only when unset. Root cause (module-level process.exit on import) revisited in Phase 3.

Title: `npm run lint` cannot run: apps/web has no ESLint config so `next lint` stops at an interactive setup prompt and exits 1
Expected: Lint runs non-interactively and reports findings
Actual: `? How would you like to configure ESLint?` prompt → `npm error Lifecycle script lint failed` (exit 1). Lint is not part of CI so this was never noticed.
Notes: Fix: apps/web/.eslintrc.json (next/core-web-vitals) + eslint@8.57.1, eslint-config-next@14.2.35. Now 0 errors, 3 warnings (react-hooks/exhaustive-deps). api/shared/mobile still have no lint → Phase 3 (strict config).

Title: Access token remains valid for up to 15 min after logout
Environment: E1 local, API dist build on :4100, seed data
Repro steps:
1. POST /auth/login as cashier@canavo.local → accessToken A, refreshToken F
2. POST /auth/logout {refreshToken: F} → 204
3. GET /auth/me with `Authorization: Bearer A`
Expected: 401 — a logged-out session can no longer be used (brief P8 'logout invalidation')
Actual: 200 with the user profile. Logout revokes only the refresh-token family; the stateless JWT stays valid until expiry (ACCESS_TTL 15 min). Same applies to a stolen token after the user logs out on a shared POS terminal.
Notes: Options: (a) bump tokenVersion on logout (logs out ALL devices of the user); (b) per-session id (sid) claim checked against the refresh family, revoked on logout (per-device); (c) accept risk + shorten TTL to 5 min. Recommend (b). Changes auth behaviour → asking before implementing.
